publisher_issuer: ContextLogic Inc. (Wish) (filed with U.S. SEC, EDGAR CIK 0001822250)
company_context: ContextLogic operated the Wish e-commerce marketplace, which scaled rapidly on cheap, paid digital-ad-driven user acquisition. After its December 2020 IPO, user engagement collapsed as advertising efficiency fell and pandemic tailwinds reversed.
macro_context: Post-pandemic reopening reduced mobile shopping time; Apple iOS privacy (ATT) changes raised digital advertising costs and reduced targeting efficiency, intensifying competition for ad impressions.
evidence_summary: Wish's growth depended on heavy paid digital advertising to acquire and re-engage low-intent buyers. In 2020 sales and marketing expense was approximately $1.7 billion. When iOS privacy changes and reopening drove advertising costs up and mobile usage down, monthly active users and active buyers fell sharply (MAUs down ~22% YoY by Q2 2021; active buyers down ~26% YoY to ~52 million in Q2 2021), and revenue plunged. The acquisition channel that built the marketplace became uneconomic and the user base eroded.
owner_decision_context: Management had built distribution almost entirely on bought traffic. Facing surging ad costs and falling efficiency, leadership had to decide whether to keep spending into a deteriorating-ROI channel or cut spend (which accelerated user decline). They reduced marketing in 2021 (~$1.1B vs ~$1.7B in 2020), and the user base contracted.
action_taken: Reduced sales and marketing spend in 2021 and attempted product/merchant-quality improvements and a later rebrand; user and revenue erosion continued.
outcome_evidence: MAUs (-~22% YoY) and active buyers (-~26% YoY to ~52M in Q2 2021) declined alongside steep revenue decline, confirming that demand was channel-dependent and collapsed when the paid-acquisition channel lost efficiency.
source_limitations: WebFetch of sec.gov returned HTTP 403. Figures confirmed in WebSearch snippets attributed to the 2020/2021 10-K and 10-Q filings and corroborated by named outlets. Some metrics are quarterly (Q2 2021) rather than full-year; the $1.1B vs $1.7B sales-and-marketing figures are company-reported annual amounts. Full-year 2021 net loss and revenue figures were not cleanly confirmable from primary snippets and are omitted.
directly_stated: 2020 sales and marketing expense was approximately $1.7 billion (~$1,708M)
2021 sales and marketing expense was approximately $1.1 billion (~$1,102M)
MAUs declined approximately 22% YoY as of Q2 2021, attributed to easing stay-at-home restrictions and lower marketing efficiency as digital ad costs rose
Active buyers fell to approximately 52 million in Q2 2021, down ~26% YoY
inferred: The marketplace's demand was structurally dependent on paid digital advertising (GTM channel mismatch)
iOS privacy changes acting as an exogenous shock to the core acquisition channel triggered the demand collapse
why_useful_for_opsiq: Demonstrates a paid-acquisition-dependent marketplace whose demand collapsed when its single dominant channel lost efficiency due to an external shock (iOS ATT) plus reopening. Tests whether the engine identifies channel/acquisition dependence (gtm_channel_mismatch) versus a generic demand-collapse narrative, and whether it routes an external shock into re-evaluation.
